steps.output: Solved task-758bec8c from four demos. Inputs have sparse plus-shaped objects: arms are color 3, centers are digits, and sometimes a hollow plus has center 0. Extend each numbered center's color along its row and column, but stop a ray at the first color-3 arm belonging to another plus; keep that 3 and do not paint beyond it. A source ray passes its own 3 arms. Preserve all original 3s. Where horizontal and vertical colored rays cross, the vertical ray wins. A hollow (0-centered) plus can leave a zero hole on its column across horizontal colored rays; the colored vertical rays still overlay its row. In practice, compute horizontal rays first, then vertical rays, preserving 3 markers and respecting foreign-marker stops. Demonstrations showed e.g. a vertical ray stopped above/below at another object's arm, and 2's horizontal line had no fill beyond another plus's 3 marker. This refinement fixed prior mistaken full-row/full-column fills.
